reason: Selected graph-repair and replanning comparisons support a division between mechanically implied repair and semantic replanning in symbolic simulation.

candidates.title: Repair modeled action errors before asking the LLM to replan
candidates.rule: When an explicit action model determines a failed plan’s correction, compare direct graph-derived repair with sending every failure back to the LLM; reserve replanning for unresolved semantic errors.
candidates.passage: graph repairs and never re-queries the LLM
candidates.location: Section V-E, Table I; V-F, Table II
candidates.finding: For Qwen3-4B single-task planning, graph-only repair reaches 67.7% versus 55.4% feedback-only replanning, using fewer model calls. Combining graph repair and selective semantic replanning reaches 88.8%.
candidates.conditions: World model represents object relations, action preconditions/effects and relevant beliefs. Comparisons use the same symbolic task environment.
candidates.limitations: Graph correctness and instruction grounding remain prerequisites. Symbolic manipulation omits geometric feasibility, reachability and collisions, so these figures are not physical-robot safety validation.
candidates.validation_test: Compare feedback-only, graph-only and hybrid repair on held-out modeled tasks; separately inject grounding and world-model errors and measure success, calls, latency and unsafe proposed actions.

candidates.title: Reorder independent subtasks as location beliefs change
candidates.rule: For partially observed multi-task planning, compare fixed or point-estimate ordering with distribution-aware ordering that is recomputed after new observations.
candidates.passage: online reordering after each completed task further reduces it to 78.01 m.
candidates.finding: With Qwen3-8B, distributional ordering reduces travel from 82.45m for map-only to 79.69m for static distributional ordering; online reordering reduces it further to 78.01m with unchanged reported success.
candidates.conditions: Travel comparisons use matched successful sets; graph beliefs represent unobserved object locations and permit task reordering.
candidates.limitations: The combined 5.4% reduction is relative to map-only, not the marginal online-versus-static gain. Symbolic settings omit geometric feasibility; room-type priors may be wrong. Dependencies must remain satisfied when reordering.
candidates.validation_test: Compare fixed, point-estimate, static-distributional and online-distributional schedules on the same tasks; report travel on matched successes, failures and planning overhead.

review_scope: Selected abstract, introduction, methods or main-result sections; not a comprehensive paper or appendix review.
